subject: Data processing regions, subprocessors, and deletion workflow — prospect Q&A
messages:
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@stellarpay.com>
To: monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: StellarPay Legal <legal@stellarpay.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Questions on where data is processed and deletion guarantees

Hi Monica,

Thanks for the demo last week — appreciated the walkthrough of routing policies. We have a few follow-ups from our security and legal teams before we proceed to procurement:

1) For EU customers, can you confirm which cloud regions or on-prem sites customer request data and model artifacts are processed in? Are there any secondary processing hops (e.g., logging, analytics) that go outside the EU?

2) Which subprocessors are involved in the request path (inference runtime, monitoring, logging, observability, metrics)? We need names and country locations where those subprocessors process or store logs for an EU-deployed workload.

3) If StellarPay pins to an EU-only Dedicated instance, are there any circumstances under which requests or cached KV data would be transferred outside the EU (e.g., fallback to U.S. model variants, emergency routing)?

4) Please outline your deletion workflow and timelines for request logs, KV cache, and model runtimes — what guarantees do you provide and how are they triggered (API, retention TTL, account termination)?

Attached is the RFP excerpt for reference (StellarPay_RFP.pdf). If it helps, happy to do a short call later today to walk through.

Best,
Alex
Director of Security, StellarPay

From: monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@stellarpay.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, evelyn_hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Questions on where data is processed and deletion guarantees

Hi Alex — thanks, and great questions. I pulled together concise answers below and attached a data-flow diagram to show routing decisions. Happy to jump on a 30-min call if you prefer to walk these through.

1) Regions and processing hops
- Primary inference and request handling for EU Dedicated customers occurs in customer-selected EU cloud regions (currently Azure West Europe and GCP Europe-west).
- Control-plane telemetry (usage metrics and billing metadata) is routed to our EU control-plane endpoints when the account is EU-resident; we do not export control-plane telemetry to the U.S. for EU-resident accounts as part of normal operation.
- Ancillary analytics (aggregated product telemetry used for capacity planning) is processed in EU-only locations for EU accounts unless explicit opt-in is given.

2) Subprocessors and locations
- Inference runtime: Our managed runtime (Redwood Runtime) runs on customer-dedicated GPU pools in the selected cloud region (no processing in other regions by default).
- Monitoring & metrics: Prometheus & Grafana hosted by Redwood in EU regions (data retention for metrics is aggregated; raw logs are minimized).
- Logging and audit trail: Structured audit logs for EU accounts are retained in EU-hosted object storage (S3/GCS equivalents in-region). We use a managed object storage provider (cloud vendor regional service) and a third-party log-indexing partner for support cases — all contractually restricted to EU processing for EU accounts.
- Subprocessor list (high level): cloud infra provider (region-specific), managed log indexer (EU-only for EU accounts), telemetry aggregator (EU), optional third-party alerting (EU). Full DPA subprocessor list will be provided in onboarding paperwork.

3) Fallbacks and cross-border transfer scenarios
- Default: No cross-border transfers for in-flight requests or KV caches for EU-dedicated instances.
- Fallbacks: We have capacity-fallback policies that are transparent — by default we will not route EU-dedicated traffic outside the EU. In a documented emergency (e.g., complete region outage and customer-approved fallback), requests could be routed to a compatible region; such routing requires explicit enrollment or written authorization.

4) Deletion workflow and SLAs
- Request logs: Can be deleted via API or by retention TTL. Standard retention is 90 days; customers can request shorter retention during onboarding. Deletion requests are processed within 48 hours and purged from object storage within 30 days (garbage collection window).
- KV cache: Per-customer KV caches are tied to the instance and removed on instance termination or by explicit API call. Cache entries are encrypted at rest; deletion is immediate from runtime and garbage-collected from underlying storage within 7 days.
- Model artifacts: Model binaries are versioned; when a customer requests model removal or a model variant is deprecated for an account, binaries are removed from customer-assigned stores within 30 days; backups follow the same retention.
- Audit: We provide signed deletion confirmations for account termination and upon request for compliance audits.

Im looping in Ben for any additional infra/engineering detail you might need.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@stellarpay.com>
Cc: evelyn_hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, dev_patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 12:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Questions on where data is processed and deletion guarantees

Alex, quick add from infra side:

- KV caching details: KV cache is scoped per customer and per model version. It lives in encrypted ephemeral volumes attached to the runtime node. For Dedicated EU instances we use in-region block storage; snapshots are disabled unless explicitly requested.
- Logs: Application logs contain request ids and metrics; PII is redacted at the agent layer before logging. Raw request payloads are not retained in the metrics pipeline.
- Subprocessors: the specific vendor names we use for log indexing and alerting (for EU accounts) are listed in the DPA we send during procurement (we limit to EU-based providers for EU accounts). If your procurement team needs vendor addresses for the security questionnaire, we can provide a signed vendor addendum.

If you want, we can arrange a short session with Evelyn (Privacy) to go through the deletion confirmation flow and the signed evidence you require.

-Ben
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@stellarpay.com>

Subject: Re: Questions on where data is processed and deletion guarantees

Thanks — this is very helpful. A couple quick follow-ups before we schedule a call:

- Can you confirm the maximum SLA for deletion confirmation (signed evidence) once requested by procurement? We need a maximum 14-day window in our contract language.
- For the DPA subprocessor list, can you provide the vendor legal names and countries (not just a function-level description)? Our legal team flagged that requirement.

If you can provide those two items via reply or the shared Drive link, well review and then propose times to meet.

Best,
Alex
Director of Security, StellarPay
